title: Cross-domain lane reservations and nighttime-deploy safehold playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As we scale regional launches and support mixed hosted/dedicated/private rollouts, teams are tripping over conflicting launch slots and nighttime deployment windows. The result: unplanned capacity contention, manual coordination overhead, and noisy rollbacks across runtime and console surfaces.

Goal: Define a lightweight, prescriptive playbook for reserving cross-domain lanes (runtime, console, API) and an automated safehold for nighttime deploys that preserves critical SLOs while minimizing manual triage. This ticket scopes the PM-owned playbook, coordinating engineering runbooks, and a small Console UI placeholder for lane occupancy visibility.

Scope:
- Define lane reservation primitives (duration, capacity token, tenant isolation rules) and owner contract.
- Create rollout-safehold rules that automatically pause non-critical release trains during overnight windows if latency or error budgets cross thresholds.
- Build a minimal Console view (read-only) that surfaces lane reservations and active safeholds.
- Author cross-functional runbook: preflight checklist, cutover and rollback triggers, communication template, and post-mortem anchors.
- Coordinate required runtime autoscaling and routing feature flags to ensure safehold enforcement (engineering work tracked separately).

Out of scope: full feature implementation for automatic lane booking in Calendar-as-Code; complex billing or quota adjustments — those will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with owner, steps, and examples
Safehold rules and thresholds approved by SRE and Runtime leads
Console read-only view prototype available behind feature flag
Two simulated dry-run exercises completed with checklist and roll-forward/rollback metrics captured
milestones: M1: Draft playbook and owner matrix (2026-03-01)
M2: Alignment with Runtime/SRE and Console teams (2026-03-15)
M4: Two dry-run exercises and adjustments (2026-04-20)
M5: Publish final playbook and retro (2026-04-30)
risks: Automation scope creep — keep Console changes minimal to avoid delaying playbook
Ambiguous owner boundaries between Dedicated and Private deployments for lane enforcement
Nighttime safehold false-positives could block critical hotfixes without fast-override paths
Dependencies on runtime metrics and alerting accuracy — SRE buy-in required
